correctness.rationale: The three stationary equations form a nonsingular linear system (determinant -314/25), giving x=25(7t-3)/(157t), y=(703-175t)/(2512t), z=(97-17t)/(2512t). Positivity is equivalent to 3/7<t<703/175. Independently expanded the Jacobian cubic and verified its A,B,C, with H=AB-C equal to the stated quartic Q divided by 7925540864 t^3. The B numerator has negative discriminant and its unique real root is negative. Descartes signs and disjoint rational sign brackets imply precisely three positive Q-roots, of which only two are feasible. At each, (lambda+A)(lambda^2+B) and nonzero H-prime yield simple transversal imaginary crossings, first destabilizing then restabilizing. These are spectral/local results only; the nonlinear Hopf Lyapunov coefficient is not established.

value.rationale: A rigorously isolated stable–unstable–stable reentrance of a positive three-species coexistence equilibrium under one physically interpretable predator-conversion parameter provides a motivated boundary example in competitive ecology. Exact open robustness and opposite transverse oscillatory crossings, not textbook application alone, are the useful findings.

limitations: Unique positive coexistence equilibrium only; local spectral/exponential stability; no global attractor or nonlinear Hopf branch claimed. Identified exact rates are a constructed example, not optimized.
